verses.zh: 所罗门就在耶路撒冷、耶和华向他父大卫显现的摩利亚山上，就是耶布斯人阿珥楠的禾场上、大卫所指定的地方预备好了，开工建造耶和华的殿。
verses.en: Solomon began building the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] on Mount Moriah, where the Lord[NOTE:2] had appeared to his father David. This was the place that David prepared at the threshing floor of Ornan[NOTE:3] the Jebusite.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “where he.” “Lord” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
In 2 Sam 24:16 this individual is called אֲרַוְנָא (ʾaravna; traditionally “Araunah”). The form of the name found here also occurs in 1 Chr 21:15; 18-28.
verses.commentary:
3:1 Josephus, Antiq. 8.3.1-3 tells of this building project.

"Mount Moriah" This was one of the seven hills of Jerusalem. It was the site of the offering of Isaac (cf. Gen. 32:2,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

"where the Lord appeared to his father David" This event is recorded in
1 Chronicles 18.

David is connected to the temple in several ways.

- He wanted to build the temple ‒ 2 Samuel 7.

- He designed the overall plan.

- He gathered the materials (using Hiram)

- He was directed by YHWH where to build it.

"Ornan the Jebusite" In 2 Sam. 24:16 he is called "Araunah the Jebusite." However, in 1 Chr. 21:15,18-27,28,
he goes by "Ornan" (BDB 75).

verses.zh: 所罗门作王第四年二月初二日开工建造。
verses.en: He began building on the second day of the second month of the fourth year of his reign.[NOTE:1]
notes: This would be April-May, 966 b.c. by modern reckoning.
verses.commentary:
3:2 The proposed date would be the spring of 966 b.c. (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS

verses.zh: 所罗门建筑　神殿的根基，乃是这样：长六十肘，宽二十肘，都按着古时的尺寸。
verses.en: Solomon laid the foundation for God’s temple;[NOTE:1] its length (determined according to the old standard of measure) was 90 feet, and its width 30 feet.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and these are the founding of Solomon to build the house of God.”

Heb “the length [in] cubits by the former measure was 60 cubits, and a width of 20 cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches (45 cm) for the standard cubit, the length of the foundation would be 90 feet (27 m) and its width 30 feet (9 m).
verses.commentary:
3:3 "cubits" The description of the temple here is a summary of 1 Kings 6-7. Much needed information

- has been left out

- is in "technical" terms

- purposeful hyperbole that the ancient versions did not understand.

For a good brief discussion see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 313-321.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT

verses.zh: 殿前的廊子长二十肘，与殿的宽窄一样，高一百二十肘；里面贴上精金。
verses.en: The porch in front of the main hall was 30 feet long, corresponding to the width of the temple,[NOTE:1] and its height was 30 feet.[NOTE:2] He plated the inside with pure gold.
notes: Heb “and the porch which was in front of the length corresponding to the width of the house, 20 cubits.” The phrase הֵיכַל הַבַּיִת (hekhal habbayit, “the main hall of the temple,” which appears in the parallel account in 1 Kgs 6:3) has been accidentally omitted by homoioarcton after עַל־פְּנֵי (’al pene, “in front of”). Note that the following form, הָאֹרֶךְ (haʿorekh, “the length”), also begins with the Hebrew letter he (ה). A scribe’s eye probably jumped from the initial he on הֵיכַל to the initial he on הָאֹרֶךְ, leaving out the intervening letters in the process.

The Hebrew text has “one hundred and 20 cubits,” i.e., (assuming a cubit of 18 inches) 180 feet (54 m). An ancient Greek witness and the Syriac version read “20 cubits,” i.e., 30 feet (9 m). It is likely that מֵאָה (meʾah, “a hundred”) should be emended to אַמּוֹת (ʾammot, “cubits”).
verses.commentary:
3:4

NASB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"the porch"

NKJV, NRSV, REB
"the vestibule"

TEV
"entrance room"

NJB
"the portico"

LXX
"an ailam"

The "porch" (BDB 17) was an added feature of Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kg. 6:3; 7:6,12,19,21;
Ezek. 8:16). It was part of David's plan (cf. 1 Chr. 28:11). It was also part of Ezekiel's new temple (cf. Ezek. 40:7,8,48,49; 41:25,26).

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, LXX
"the height 120"

TEV
"180 feet high"

REB, Peshitta, NIV
"20"

The UBS Text Project gives "120" a "B" rating (i.e., some doubt). However, it seems a more realistic
measurement is found in 1 Kgs. 6:3, where the porch is measured as 20 cubits by 10 cubits, but the height is not mentioned.
The JPSOA diagram, p. 1769, says it was "three stories" tall. However, the "bronze pillars" are only 27' (i.e., 18 cubits) tall
(cf. 1 Kgs. 7:15; 2 Kgs. 25:17; Jer. 52:21).

The MT has the pillars as "thirty five cubits" high (cf. 2 Chr. 3:15), which is 52.5 feet. The NET Bible, p. 671,
#9, suggests that a scribe misread "cubit" as "hundred."

"he overlaid it with pure gold" The NASB Study Bible, p. 592, suggests that the VERB "overlaid"
(BDB 860, KB 1045, Piel IMPERFECT with waw, cf. 2 Chr. 3:6,10) may denote "inlaid,"
referring to the items of 3:5. A different VERB (BDB 341, KB 339, Piel IMPERFECT
with waw) is used in 2 Chr. 3:5,7,8,9.

In the tabernacle, gold was limited to the "holy of holies," while silver was used for the "holy place" and
bronze for the laver and altar of sacrifice. But in Solomon's temple gold was used in more places.

verses.zh: 大殿的墙都用松木板遮蔽，又贴了精金，上面雕刻棕树和链子；
verses.en: He paneled[NOTE:1] the main hall[NOTE:2] with boards made from evergreen trees[NOTE:3] and plated it with fine gold, decorated with palm trees and chains.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “covered.”
Heb “the large house.”
Heb “wood of evergreens.”
Heb “and he put up on it palm trees and chains.”
verses.commentary:
3:5 "palm trees and chains" The decorations of the temple employed

- palm trees (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:29,32; 7:36; Ezek. 40:16)

- chains, 2 Chr. 3:5,16 (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:17)

- pomegranates, 2 Chr. 3:16 (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:42)

- cherubim

- in the wall hangings (1 Kgs. 7:27-39)

- carved into wood, 2 Chr. 3:7; 1 Kgs. 6:29,35

- two large ones in the holy of holies covering the ark, 2 Chr. 3:10-14; 1 Kgs. 6:23-28

- on the lid of the ark, facing each other, Exod. 25:18-20; Num. 7:89

- although not mentioned in this context, 1 Kgs. 6:29,32 also mentions "open flowers," which may refer to the menorah's
seven flower-shaped tops

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

verses.zh: 又用宝石装饰殿墙，使殿华美；所用的金子都是巴瓦音的金子。
verses.en: He decorated the temple with precious stones; the gold he used came from Parvaim.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he plated the house [with] precious stone for beauty, and the gold was the gold of Parvaim.”sn The location of Parvaim, the source of the gold for Solomon’s temple, is uncertain. Some have identified it with modern Farwa in Yemen; others relate it to the Sanskrit parvam and understand it to be a general term for the regions east of Israel.
verses.commentary:
3:6 "he adorned the house with precious stones" There are texts that tell us

- what kind of stones (1 Chr. 29:2)

- where they were placed (1 Kgs. 5:17; 7:9,10,11)

Some have suggested "inlaid floors." Like the gold, these gems were a way to show the value, worth, and
glory of YHWH's temple.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA, REB, Targums
"Parvaim"

LXX
"Pharouaim"

Peshitta, Vulgate
"fine gold"

Obviously modern translations and the LXX think it is a place name.

- northeastern Arabia (JPSOA)

- southeast Arabia (NASB Study Bible)

- Yemen

- mythological (i.e., Gaden of Righteousness, Enoch 60:23)

- rabbinical Midrash, home of Enoch (Gen. 5:21-23)

- another name for Ophir (2 Chr. 8:18)

The suggestion of the Peshitta aand Vulgate of "fine" gold seems unusual, since the adjective "pure" gold
is mentioned in 2 Chr. 3:4 (BDB 373) and "fine" gold (BDB 373 II) in 3:5,8. The exact distinction between these types of gold
is unstated.

verses.zh: 又用金子贴殿和殿的栋梁、门槛、墙壁、门扇；墙上雕刻基路伯。
verses.en: He overlaid the temple’s rafters, thresholds, walls and doors with gold; he carved decorative cherubim on the walls.

verses.zh: 又建造至圣所，长二十肘，与殿的宽窄一样，宽也是二十肘；贴上精金，共用金子六百他连得。
verses.en: He made the Most Holy Place;[NOTE:1] its length was 30 feet,[NOTE:2] corresponding to the width of the temple, and its width 30 feet.[NOTE:3] He plated it with 600 talents[NOTE:4] of fine gold.
notes: Heb “the house of the holy place of holy places.”
Heb “20 cubits.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), this would give a length of 30 feet (9 m).
Heb “20 cubits.” Some suggest adding, “and its height 20 cubits” (see 1 Kgs 6:20). The phrase could have been omitted by homoioteleuton.

The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold plating was 40,380 lbs. (18,360 kg).
verses.commentary:
3:8 "holy of holies" This was the innermost part of the tabernacle/temple. It was shaped as a perfect cube
(i.e., 20x20x20 cubits; this would make the dimensions of 2 Chr. 3:4, "120 cubits high" a scribal error). This is where the ark of
the covenant rested. Only the High Priest, on the Day of Atonement (cf. Leviticus 16), could enter this sacred place where
YHWH dwelt above the cherubim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE (chart)

verses.zh: 金钉重五十舍客勒。楼房都贴上金子。
verses.en: The gold nails weighed 50 shekels; he also plated the upper areas with gold.
verses.commentary:
3:9 The NASB Study Bible, p. 592, has a good note:

"The fact that gold is such a soft metal would make it unlikely that nails were made of this substance. It is probable
that this small amount (only 1 1/4 pounds) represents gold leaf or sheeting used to gild the nail heads."

"the upper rooms" One wonders if the perfect cube (20x20x20 cubits) caused a space above the Holy of Holies.
This is all speculation based on an assumed height of the building (i.e., "thirty cubits," 1 Kgs. 6:2).

These "upper rooms" are mentioned as being planned by David (cf. 1 Chr. 28:11).

verses.zh: 在至圣所按造像的法子造两个基路伯，用金子包裹。
verses.en: In the Most Holy Place he made two images of cherubim and plated them with gold.
verses.commentary:
3:10

NASB, JPSOA
"sculptured"

NKJV
"fashioned by carving"

NRSV, REB
"carved"

TEV
"made out of metal"

NJB
"modeled. . .of wrought metal work"

LXX
"fashioned. . .out of wood"

This is a NOUN CONSTRUCT (BDB 795 plus BDB 847). The NOUN
(BDB 795) is a common word for "deed" or "work." Here, of "a work of art."

The other NOUN (BDB 847) occurs only here. It is from an Arabic root, "things formed."
The MT is not specific whether the cherubim are fashioned from

- metal (TEV, NJB; AB, p. 15)

- wood (LXX, NKJV, NRSV, REB)

Whichever, it was overlaid with gold.

verses.zh: 两个基路伯的翅膀共长二十肘。这基路伯的一个翅膀长五肘，挨着殿这边的墙；那一个翅膀也长五肘，与那基路伯翅膀相接。
verses.en: The combined wing span of the cherubim was 30 feet.[NOTE:1] One of the first cherub’s wings was 7½ feet long and touched one wall of the temple; its other wing was also 7½ feet long and touched one of the second cherub’s wings.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the wings of the cherubim, their length was 20 cubits.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), the wingspan of the cherubim would have been 30 feet (9 m).

Heb “the wing of the one was 5 cubits from the touching of the wall of the house, and the other wing was 5 cubits from the touching of the wing of the other cherub.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), each wing would have been 7.5 feet (2.25 m) long.

verses.zh: 那基路伯的一个翅膀长五肘，挨着殿那边的墙；那一个翅膀也长五肘，与这基路伯的翅膀相接。
verses.en: Likewise one of the second cherub’s wings was 7½ feet long and touched the other wall of the temple; its other wing was also 7½ feet long and touched one of the first cherub’s wings.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the wing of the one (הָאֶחָד, haʾekhad, “the one”; this should probably be emended to הָאַחֵר, haʾakher, “the other”) cherub was 5 cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was 5 cubits, clinging to the wing of the other cherub.”

verses.zh: 两个基路伯张开翅膀，共长二十肘，面向外殿而立。
verses.en: The combined wingspan of these cherubim was 30 feet.[NOTE:1] They stood upright, facing inward.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the wings of these cherubim were spreading 20 cubits.”
Heb “and they were standing on their feet, with their faces to the house.” An alternative translation of the last clause would be, “with their faces to the main hall.”
verses.commentary:
3:13 "they stood on their feet" This clearly shows that there was a second pair of cherubim. The ones on the
lid of the ark were kneeling.

"facing the main room" This would refer to the larger room, the Holy Place (i.e., twice as long). These angels
stood as guardians (i.e., Gen. 3:24). The two cherubim on the ark faced each other, watching the "mercy seat" (i.e., the
place of atonement, cf. Leviticus 16).

verses.zh: 又用蓝色、紫色、朱红色线和细麻织幔子，在其上绣出基路伯来。
verses.en: He made the curtain out of blue, purple, crimson, and white fabrics, and embroidered on it decorative cherubim.
verses.commentary:
3:14 "the veil" This could refer to

- a room-dividing curtain; this one between the "holy of holies" and the Holy Place (cf. Exod. 36:35-38)

- a canopy suspended above the ark of the covenant

For the colors, see note at 2 Chr. 2:7.

In Solomon's temple the inner shrine (i.e., Holy of Holies and Holy Place) was divided by a door of olive
wood (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 在殿前造了两根柱子，高三十五肘；每柱顶高五肘。
verses.en: In front of the temple he made two pillars which had a combined length[NOTE:1] of 52½ feet,[NOTE:2] with each having a plated capital 7½ feet high.[NOTE:3]
notes: The figure given here appears to refer to the combined length of both pillars (perhaps when laid end-to-end on the ground prior to being set up; cf. v. 17); the figure given for the height of the pillars in 1 Kgs 7:15, 2 Kgs 25:17, and Jer 52:21 is half this (i.e., 18 cubits).
The Syriac reads “18 cubits” (27 feet). This apparently reflects an attempt at harmonization with 1 Kgs 7:15, 2 Kgs 25:17, and Jer 52:21.

Heb “and he made before the house two pillars, 35 cubits [in] length, and the plated capital which was on its top [was] 5 cubits.” The significance of the measure “35 cubits” (52.5 feet or 15.75 m, assuming a cubit of 18 inches) for the “length” of the pillars is uncertain. According to 1 Kgs 7:15, each pillar was 18 cubits (27 feet or 8.1 m) high. Perhaps the measurement given here was taken with the pillars lying end-to-end on the ground before they were set up.
verses.commentary:
3:15-17 These are the two bronze pillars that stood at the entrance of the Holy Place (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:15-22).

3:15 "thirty-five cubits high" The NET Bible suggests this was the length of both of them lying on the ground,
p. 671, #24,26. 1 Kings 7:15 and 2 Kgs. 25:17 say their height was 18 cubits.

verses.zh: 又照圣所内链子的样式做链子，安在柱顶上；又做一百石榴，安在链子上。
verses.en: He made ornamental chains[NOTE:1] and put them on top of the pillars. He also made 100 pomegranate-shaped ornaments and arranged them within the chains.
notes: The Hebrew text adds here, “in the inner sanctuary,” but the description at this point is of the pillars, not the inner sanctuary.
verses.commentary:
3:16 "chains" These are also mentioned in 1 Kgs. 7:17.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"the inner sanctuary"

NRSV, TEV, REB
--- omitted ---

NJB
"in the Debir"

A NOUN (BDB 184 I, KB 208 I), which is defined as "hindmost chamber" or
"innermost room," from an Arabic root, "back" or "behind" (KB 209 I).

However, the Hebrew word "debar" (BDB 182, KB 210 II) is the common root for "speech" or "word."
This may be a designation of the room from which YHWH speaks (cf. Num. 7:89), from above the wings of the cherubim
on the lid of the ark.

It must be noted that "inner sanctuary" (i.e., second suggestion) does not fit this context, which is talking
about the twin bronze pillars before the porch of the Holy Place.

verses.zh: 将两根柱子立在殿前，一根在右边，一根在左边；右边的起名叫雅斤，左边的起名叫波阿斯。
verses.en: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right side and the other on the left.[NOTE:1] He named the one on the right Yakin[NOTE:2] and the one on the left Boaz.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “one on the south and the other on the north.”
The name “Yakin” appears to be a verbal form and probably means, “he establishes.”

The meaning of the name “Boaz” is uncertain. For various proposals, see BDB 126-27 s.v. בֹּעַז. One attractive option is to revocalize the name as בְּעֹז (beʿoz, “in strength”) and to understand it as completing the verbal form on the first pillar. Taking the words together and reading from right to left, one can translate the sentence, “he establishes [it] in strength.”
verses.commentary:
3:17 "Jachin" This proper name (BDB 467, KB 410) for the right bronze pillar may mean "he will establish."

"Boaz" This proper name (BDB 126, KB 142 II) for the left bronze pillar may mean "quickness" or "strength."
Some scholars assume that the writing on the two pillars are one phrase, "he establishes in strength."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Where else in the OT is Mt. Moriah mentioned? Why was it chosen as the site of the temple?

- Were there two kinds of cubit? How long was a cubit?

- Describe a cherub. What was their purpose in temple art?

- Do 1 Kings 6-7 and this chapter give us a complete picture of Solomon's temple? Could we reproduce it by these measurements?

- Was there a veil or a door between the Holy of Holies and the Holy Place?

- What was the purpose of the bronze pillars?

where the Lord had appeared to his father David, at the place that David had prepared on the
